title: Bridgepoint - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Intro call to understand Bridgepoint's ML inference needs. They run customer-facing LLM assistants and need reserved GPU capacity with predictable latency and data isolation. Main constraints: PCI/regulatory data, SSO/SAML, KMS, and cost control; interested in Dedicated with Private option for VPC. Next steps: send pricing, security / SOC2 docs, run 2-week benchmark on 2xA100 + KV cache config, schedule technical deep dive.
header:
Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Bridgepoint, Head of MLOps), Lena Ortiz (Bridgepoint, CTO), Samir Desai (Bridgepoint Infra), Priya Nair (Bridgepoint Security), Jordan Lee (Bridgepoint PM)
Recording: Fireflies transcript export
Notes: Call focused on Dedicated capacity sizing, isolation (VPC/on-prem), burst strategy and scaling expectations.
transcript: 00:00:02 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intro, Riya our SE will walk through technical questions. Michael / Lena, do you want to kick off with a quick overview of what you're trying to solve?

00:00:18 Michael Torres: Yeah thanks, Avery. So Bridgepoint's been piloting an LLM-based assistant for our payments support flow. We're hitting more traffic and we need predictable latency. Right now it's a mix of managed endpoints and a bit of self-hosted. Primary ask is reserved capacity - predictable throughput, isolation for PCI data, and a burst strategy so we don't lose availability during spikes.
00:00:42 Lena Ortiz: Also regulatory: logs retention, audit trail, and KMS integration are must-haves. We may pursue an on-prem option but likely VPC first.

00:00:55 Riya Patel: Got it. Sounds like Dedicated or Private could fit. Can you share current qps, model sizes, and latency SLOs? Even ballpark numbers help us size the cluster and recommend configs.

00:01:10 Michael Torres: Ballpark: 120 concurrent users hitting the bot at peak, about 15 qps sustained and spiky bursts up to 60 qps for 30-45 seconds. Latency target is 300-500ms 95th for short chats, for longer summarization endpoints we allow up to 1s. Models: currently using a 13B-ish open model, quantized; we may move to a 70B for higher-quality queries but that's later. Token lengths average 150 tokens per request.

00:01:42 Riya Patel: Okay that helps. For 15 sustained qps with 150 tokens on a 13B quantized model, typical guidance is X GPUs with batching and KV cache. For the burst spikes to 60 qps, we recommend a burst policy - either reserved baseline with burstable spot or pre-warmed burst pool. Are you on a cloud provider in-house or do you want Redwood-managed Dedicated in our hosted infra?

00:02:05 Samir Desai: We want data isolation; ideally Dedicated in our VPC so we control network egress. We also need SAML SSO for the console and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Is that Private or Dedicated with VPC peering?

00:02:18 Avery Chen: Good question. We have two modes: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools we manage but can be VPC peered or have customer connectivity) and Redwood Private which gives you a private control plane and can be deployed inside your VPC or on-prem. For your compliance needs (PCI, KMS) many customers choose Dedicated with VPC peering initially, and move to Private when they need on-prem or tighter network restrictions.
00:02:42 Priya Nair: For PCI we need customer-managed KMS/HSM and full access logs. Any PCI customers you can point to as references?

00:02:49 Avery Chen: We have financial customers in production - happy to share redacted reference list and SOC2 docs after this call. We support KMS integrations and can surface audit logs; for HSM we can run in Private/on-prem. I'll add that to the security packet.
00:03:02 Jordan Lee: How do upgrades/rollouts work? We can't have user-facing regressions during model switches.

00:03:08 Riya Patel: We support rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant. Plus you can pin model versions. Our Optimize toolkit helps recommend quantization and batching configs to hit latency/cost targets while preserving quality. We also run evals against your prompt set to detect regressions before a rollout.
00:03:28 Michael Torres: Cool. Cost is important - we have a budget cap. How do you handle unit economics when you reserve GPUs but don't fully utilize them?

00:03:35 Avery Chen: Two levers: autoscaling policies and a burst pool. You commit to baseline capacity (reserved) for predictable throughput and price, then we configure burst capacity for short spikes which uses either pooled spare capacity or pre-warmed nodes at a lower price. We can model expected utilization and tradeoffs - we'll share a cost model spreadsheet. Also Optimize suggests batching and prefix caching to reduce token counts effectively.
00:04:01 Priya Nair: About caching - is KV cache secure? Does it store PII? We need controls to avoid sensitive data being cached long-term.

00:04:10 Riya Patel: Good question. KV cache is configurable per route; you can disable caching for sensitive paths or set TTLs and encrypt cached keys with your KMS. We'll document defaults and options in the security packet.
00:04:24 Lena Ortiz: For scaling, what's the typical cold start for a new node with a 13B or 70B model? We need to know how fast burst capacity can come up.

00:04:33 Riya Patel: Cold start depends on model size and quantization. For a 13B quantized model, warm up can be sub-minute with pre-warmed pipelines; a 70B can be several minutes without pre-warm. That's why customers use a small always-on baseline and a pre-warmed burst pool for 70B. We can also use model sharding and kernel optimizations to reduce startup time.
00:04:51 Michael Torres: We may start with 13B for now and add 70B for higher-quality paths. For the burst - can Redwood auto-failover to a cheaper model if capacity is constrained?

00:05:00 Avery Chen: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to a compatible smaller model to keep availability while preserving cost. You define tolerance for downgrade and routes that can be degraded.
00:05:10 Jordan Lee: Will we be able to run controlled benchmarks? We want to simulate 60 qps bursts and see p95 latency and token cost.

00:05:16 Riya Patel: Absolutely. Typical POC flow is: 1) Redwood runs a benchmark in our staging with 2xA100 or equivalent using your prompt set; 2) we test prefix caching and batching; 3) provide detailed token/cost/latency breakdown. We often do a 2-week pilot to capture realistic traffic patterns.
00:05:30 Michael Torres: What about SLAs? We need 99.9% availability for production endpoints.

00:05:36 Avery Chen: Dedicated plans can include SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. For ultra-critical workloads, Private deployment with a regional redundant architecture can help. We'll include SLA options in the pricing packet.
00:05:46 Priya Nair: On compliance: do you support SAML, SSO, RBAC, audit logs retention and sending logs to Splunk or our SIEM?
00:05:54 Avery Chen: Yes to all - SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, retention policies, and push logs to customer endpoints. We'll share configuration docs and examples.
00:06:05 Samir Desai: Networking: do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink for the control plane? We want minimal public egress.

00:06:12 Riya Patel: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink-like setups, and air-gapped on-prem for Private customers. For Dedicated, we can set up peering and NAT rules so inference traffic doesn't traverse public internet.
00:06:24 Michael Torres: Any performance tuning recommendations for our infra - L4 load balancers, TLS termination, tokenization on client side?

00:06:31 Riya Patel: We usually recommend client-side tokenization, keep request sizes small-ish, use gRPC for lower overhead if you can, and configure edge LB with consistent hashing if you need session affinity for KV cache hits. We'll include a best-practices doc.
00:06:47 Jordan Lee: Who's typically involved from Redwood during a pilot? We want clear owners.
00:06:52 Avery Chen: AE owner (me), SE lead (Riya) for benchmarks and config, and an SRE contact for infra. We'll also loop in our security/compliance SME for the paperwork.
00:07:02 Michael Torres: Timeline - we want a pilot in two weeks, with procurement on our side likely done in three weeks if security review goes well. Is that feasible?
00:07:10 Avery Chen: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll send pricing and security docs today/tomorrow. For benchmarks, can we schedule the technical deep dive next Wednesday?
00:07:18 Lena Ortiz: Next Wednesday works for us, Riya can lead the deep dive and we'll provide prompt sets and traffic traces beforehand.

00:07:25 Riya Patel: Perfect. I'll prepare an initial sizing recommendation: baseline reserve for 2xA100-equivalent for 15 qps and a pre-warmed burst pool to handle 60 qps spikes, plus a path to scale to 4xA100 if you add a 70B production path. We'll share the model and cost tradeoffs.
00:07:40 Michael Torres: One more - data residency: some customers require EU-only. We operate multi-region. Can Redwood pin deployments to region?
00:07:47 Avery Chen: Yes, you can pin regions and we support region-constrained deployments for Dedicated and Private. We'll note EU region options in the follow-up.
00:07:55 Priya Nair: Please include SOC2 report and penetration test summary in the security packet. Also want detail on encryption at rest and in transit and KMS architecture.
00:08:03 Avery Chen: Will do. We'll redact customer information where needed but include architecture diagrams.
00:08:10 Jordan Lee: Any obvious blockers you see from what we said?
00:08:13 Riya Patel: Nothing major - principal items are procurement sign-off, KMS/HSM decisions, and alignment on baseline commit. We'll help model costs to fit your budget.
00:08:21 Michael Torres: Great. If pilot looks good we'll talk committed Dedicated contracts for predictable monthly pricing.
00:08:26 Avery Chen: Sounds good. We'll follow up with next steps. I'll summarize and send notes shortly.
00:08:30 (cross-talk) Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
